We have a specification consisting of user stories U1-U8 for Hyperledger Fabric. We need to implement these features. Let's parse each user story and infer tasks.

U1: "As an application developer, I want to provide friendly name to identify a chain code, so I can more easily manage and debug chain code." This implies adding a friendly name (alias?) to chaincode identification. Need to modify chaincode metadata, lifecycle, possibly APIs, CLI, and tests.

U2: "As a chaincode developer, I want use life cycle system cc to manage deployment policies for chain codes" This implies implementing or enhancing lifecycle system chaincode to manage deployment policies. Need to define policy structures, APIs, storage, enforcement.

U3: "As an application developer, I want documentation for upgrade flows" Documentation only? Need to write upgrade flow docs. Effort for documentation.

U4: "As application developer, I want an easy way to deploy and test my app by only having a single orderer process. This refers to the 'Solo' ordering process. This will be a simple to deploy, minimal code ordering process. Because there is only one process, no 'consensus' need be reached between multiple processes, so this is largely as simple as having multiple clients write into a buffered channel, with a single thread reading it, and creating batches/blocks. The deliver side is only slightly more complicated, as to allow for disconnection and reconnection, the orderer service must allow history to be discovered. This requires implementing a simple in RAM ledger, and allowing individual clients to seek within it." So implement Solo orderer: a new ordering service implementation with in-memory ledger, buffered channel, batch creation, deliver with seek. Need to integrate with existing orderer interfaces, config, tests.

U5: "as a developer, I can find the Hyperledger Fabric code on GitHub so that I can explore it without needing access to Gerrit" This is about publishing code to GitHub, maybe mirroring from Gerrit. As a developer implementing increment, we might need to set up GitHub mirror or ensure code is pushed. But from software development perspective, maybe just ensure repo is mirrored, CI, etc. Could be operational but we can include activity to set up GitHub repository/mirror and verify code presence. Effort maybe low.

U6: "As a developer I need the ability to access a state cache so that we can help submitters quickly build the rw-set. This will also lead to better performance." This implies implementing a state cache (likely in peer/endorser) to cache state reads, helping build read-write set. Need to design cache, integrate with state database, invalidation, etc.

U7: "as a developer, I can find the hyperledger fabric documentation easily so that I can develop chaincode and applications. Ideally, the documentation for all hyperledger projects can be easily found at hyperledger.org." This is about documentation portal/website. Could be effort to publish docs to hyperledger.org or improve docs index. We can assume we need to update documentation site / add links. Low effort.

U8: "as an operator, I should have a cli that I can easily install that lets me interact with the various components of the fabric. The current peer commands are entangled with the validating peer capability, which means that building and installing a peer for Mac and Windows is complicated by the need to have RocksDB etc installed. We can extract the peer commands into a separate component that is not dependent on the internals of the peer node, that can be simply installed as a platform-specific binary." This is extracting CLI from peer into separate component (e.g., fabric-cli). Need to refactor code, create new module/binary, remove dependencies (RocksDB), build scripts for Mac/Windows, tests.

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement Solo orderer as a new package implementing the existing Orderer interface, using an in-memory ledger and a buffered Go channel with a single goroutine creating blocks.
Support deliver service with SeekOldest, SeekNewest, and Seek specific block number using the in-RAM ledger to allow disconnect/reconnect.
Add friendly chaincode name as optional metadata stored in the Lifecycle System Chaincode (LSCC) and indexed per channel.
Extend LSCC to store and retrieve deployment policies as part of chaincode instantiation and upgrade.
Implement a per-peer in-memory LRU state cache that intercepts state reads during endorsement to accelerate rw-set construction, with invalidation on block commit.
Extract CLI into a separate Go module/binary that communicates with peer and orderer via gRPC, removing dependency on peer internals and RocksDB.
Use Go cross-compilation and platform-specific packaging scripts for CLI distribution on Mac, Windows, and Linux.
Mirror the Gerrit repository to GitHub via a CI job and update README to point to GitHub for browsing.
Publish and link Fabric documentation on the hyperledger.org docs portal and provide local upgrade flow docs in the repo.
assumptions: Existing Hyperledger Fabric codebase, build tooling, and test infrastructure are available and familiar to the developer.
Solo orderer does not require persistence across restarts; an in-RAM ledger is sufficient for development and test.
State cache is process-local and not shared across peers; consistency is maintained via commit-time invalidation.
Deployment policies reuse existing policy primitives if available; otherwise a minimal signature policy format is defined.
CLI extraction targets the most commonly used peer subcommands and does not need to replicate all deprecated admin commands in this increment.
Documentation tasks cover writing or updating Markdown/static site content; no full website redesign is required.
Effort estimates reflect personal development work only and exclude external code review cycles and elapsed time for upstream merge.
All estimates are expressed in work-hours for a single experienced Go developer.
